key_insight: Adversarial Heuristic Learning lets AI agents improve game-playing policies by rewriting executable programs from experience, but top performance still depends heavily on game complexity and feedback quality.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path for building adaptive, model-agnostic game agents that can refine software behavior without retraining weights, which is useful for benchmark-driven autonomous systems.
method: Defines AHL: fixed model weights, but agents revise policies and supporting code from match experience.
Introduces AAArena with 12 authentic adversarial games and 1,920 archived human programs.
Evaluates agents under competition-like budgets for opponent choice, replay analysis, and policy updates.
evidence_signal: Across 12 games, the study reports 6 gold medals for Opus5.5 with Claude Code, while the other 6 human ladders were not topped by any evaluated configuration.
watch_item: Performance drops on games with more complex rule specifications, so gains may be limited by rule understanding and long-horizon planning.
paper_title: Can AI Agents Learn Their Way to the Top? Evaluating Heuristic Learning in a Long-Running Game Agent Competition
